analysis: Examined .github/workflows/release-provider.yml base lines 1061-1296 and head lines 1-558. The visible changes are CI/release workflow changes. They add a CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND gate (head 346-356) and docs (66-72). Qualification is split into a qualify-sdk-shard matrix (head 250-280) plus an aggregator job qualify-sdk (282-315) that checks shard suite lists. The build-and-release job requires qualify-sdk success, or skipped on resume (320-323). qualify-sdk is still the single qualification result. It uses needs: [resolve-env, qualify-sdk-shard] with no !cancelled() override, so it is skipped unless all shards succeed, and the downstream condition requires success. Credential handling is unchanged: environment-gated secret resolution (PROD_/STAGING_/LEGACY_ values empty unless the resolved environment matches), source verification on master before secrets, publication artifact id/digest-verified download. The base-side publish/stage jobs show the same patterns and gating, with concurrency groups and the older-macOS validation. The head excerpt ends at line 558, so changes at head 989-1071 and 1126-1136 (stage/publish jobs) are not visible in the supplied head text; I viewed only the base counterparts. No evidence of weakened publication, signing or qualification controls in the visible portion. Residual questions: (1) whether the audit step in provider-test-shards.py actually guarantees full-suite coverage; (2) whether the artifact pattern provider-sdk-qualification-<env>-<sha>-shard-* could match stale or foreign artifacts and whether the shard action uploads under that name (not visible); (3) the unseen head changes to stage/publish jobs and cluster_runtime registration, which the coordinator must accept (platform-owned). These relate to the release artifact integrity (A-011, A-017, T-034) and merit a pass over the rest of the diff, but no concrete regression is demonstrated.
